results.primary_cause: Available evidence is conflicting and does not provide sufficiently current, time-consistent confirmation of the exact container spot/contract freight and liner-utilization cycle as of the research date. Earlier analysis describes potential overcapacity and a downward spot-rate trajectory, while other reporting describes a changing post-Red Sea market.

supporting_evidence.claim: The container shipping market was described as facing uncertainty and potential overcapacity if Red Sea routing normalized, indicating a freight-cycle mechanism affecting industry capacity and rates.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Container Shipping: Sailing Through Uncertainty And Looming Overcapacity

supporting_evidence.claim: The container shipping market in 2025 was described as resembling the pre-Red Sea-crisis market, indicating a material shift in container spot-rate conditions and liner-cycle dynamics.
supporting_evidence.source_title: The rise and fall of container spot rates — and what it means for 2026

counter_evidence.claim: Container freight spot rates were reported to be falling, with tariff uncertainty and demand failing to match supply; blank sailings only cushioned the decline.
counter_evidence.source_title: Blank Sailings Cushion Fall for Container Spot Rates

results.primary_cause: Current 2026 evidence reports strengthening dry-bulk freight conditions, including a higher Baltic Dry Index and elevated Capesize rates tied to commodity-vessel demand and tighter vessel supply. Counter-evidence indicates that part of the strength may be rerouting-related and could reverse, but it does not negate the currently observed freight-cycle activation.

supporting_evidence.claim: The Baltic Dry Index reached 2,732 points on July 31, 2026, up approximately 9.2% during July, with dry-bulk market conditions strengthening across vessel segments.
supporting_evidence.source_title: HTCO Highlights Strengthening Dry Bulk Market as BDI Rises Approximately 9.2% in July and Shipping Equities Gain Investor Attention

supporting_evidence.claim: A key dry-bulk rate measure reached its highest level since December 2023, driven by rising Capesize demand and tightening supply of bulk carriers.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Dry-Bulk Shipping Rates Hit Two-Year High on Capesize Demand

counter_evidence.claim: BIMCO warned that apparent 2026 dry-bulk strength was substantially artificial and driven by forced rerouting, with a potential 2027 supply glut as the rerouting effect reverses.
counter_evidence.source_title: Dry bulk shipping faces 2027 supply glut: BIMCO warns Hormuz rerouting boost will reverse
